record.scientificName: Pongo tapanuliensis Nurcahyo, Meijaard, Nowak, Fredriksson & Groves in Nater et al., 2017
record.authorship: Nurcahyo, Meijaard, Nowak, Fredriksson & Groves in Nater et al., 2017

claim.text: A historical-ecology analysis of records from the early 1800s through 2009 concluded that the species' historical extent of occurrence was much larger than its remaining range: the then-current extent was estimated as 2.5% of the historical range in the 1890s and 5.0% in the 1940s. The article notes that the historical record set and location precision are incomplete; these estimates are not a present-day range survey.
claim.locator: Abstract; Methods, historical-source compilation and record reliability; Results, historical distribution and range comparison; Fig. 3 and Table 1.
claim.scope: Historical literature and museum-record analysis for Sumatra, drawing on records from the early 1800s to 2009; historical comparisons use the 1890s and 1940s. Spatial scope is attributed records south of Lake Toba and the Batang Toru region, with uncertain records discussed separately.
claim.lifeStatus: Claims concern historical wild-occurrence records attributed by the authors to Pongo tapanuliensis; uncertain or ambiguously located records are not treated as certain occurrences.

evidence.title: The historical range and drivers of decline of the Tapanuli orangutan
evidence.authors: Meijaard E, Ni'matullah S, Dennis R, Sherman J, Onrizal, Wich SA
evidence.licenseAppliesTo: The article text under its item-level open-access license; separately credited third-party figures and material are excluded.
